It is difficult to present a limited biography without making it seem fragmentary when it also, the sketch drawn from the impressions of former students, reflects so clearly his character and work. It seems appropriate, therefore, to give the sketch of the following faculty members, based on sincere expressions of appreciation which came unsolicited to the writer from his former students.

Professor Robert B. Halsell was born in Monroe County, Kentucky, September 28, 1848, and is a son of James F. and Coly (Wyatt) Halsell. The father, James F., was a physician and well-known in the community in which he lived. He moved to Texas, in Collin County, in which State he served as sheriff for several years. He was associated with the family and formed until his death in 1879, at the age of seventy-three—a Free Mason and a member of the local church. Professor Robert B. Halsell, born in Barren County, Kentucky, April 16, 1863, is still living, and is the subject of this sketch.

Robert B. Halsell, the youngest child of the above-named parents, was reared upon the farm in that part of Texas which borders on the Red River. He served in the Confederate cavalry, and served until the close of the war, when with his health. He has been a student of the Lawyers' Institute at Ladonia, since the time that Institution was chartered in 1879, and is now one of the most renowned institutions of the State.

On June 23, 1869, professor Halsell married Miss Nancy M. Scott, daughter of the Rev. and Mrs. H. P. Scott, of Barren County, Kentucky, April 16, 1863, is still living, and is the subject of this sketch.
